description: P3 consumer-assertion: `#### Transport Degradation Is a Hard Stop` in plugin/governance/security-policy.md is the CANONICAL statement that a session lacking the Write tool must stop blocked rather than improvise a shell transport for a navigator's inputs file. Eight files point at that subsection BY NAME — the seven inert inputs-file navigators (init-run-ledger, record-state-result, mark-intent-fallback, spawn-brood, seed-hive, molt, open-plan-pr) and the overlord's own transport prohibition. Renaming or deleting the subsection turns every one of those pointers into a dangling reference with nothing to fail on. This fixture pins the LINK at each consumer and NOT the canonical text those consumers used to restate: consumer patterns carry only the pointer itself, so remedy prose stays free to evolve at the canonical site without breaking a single remote assertion. THREE pieces of canonical CONTENT are pinned, all of them on security-policy.md itself, and each protects a DISTINCT claim rather than freezing prose at random. (1) The load-bearing NEGATIVE sentence stating that re-running `hivemind:seed-hive` cannot restore an absent tool: it is what separates the capability gate (TOOL ABSENT) from the prompt gate; its silent removal would reopen the defect class by letting a tool-absent session be told to re-seed instead of to stop. (2) The ADR-0017 class-elimination clause: it is the only sentence anywhere in the plugin that NAMES the class the shell-transport prohibition exists to keep closed, so it carries the entire WHY behind that prohibition; deleted, the prohibition survives as an unjustified style rule a later editor can relax without ever seeing what it was protecting. (3) The outcome-keyed trip condition: it is the normative rule the whole subsection exists to state, and it is keyed on OUTCOME rather than on any enumerated cause; deleted, only the DIAGNOSTIC cause list remains, which re-admits every unnamed cause as an implicit exception and reverts the subsection to the cause-enumerated form this feature replaced. Each assertion is scoped to ONE file and each pattern is spelled so it can only match on the side it belongs to: the source pattern carries the `####` heading marker (never present in a consumer reference), the navigator procedural pattern carries the parent-section pointer `(Inert Inputs-File Navigator Pattern →` (present only on the procedural line), and the navigator prohibition-list pattern carries the leading parenthesis `(Transport Degradation Is a Hard Stop).` (which the procedural line's unparenthesised continuation cannot satisfy). The pointer patterns above are deliberately SHORT single-line fragments — NOT because matching is line-scoped (it is not: presence matching is whitespace-normalized on BOTH sides, so a pattern MAY span a source-line wrap, and pattern (3) below deliberately does; see tests/policy/README.md rule 5) but because a consumer pin should carry only the reference itself and none of the remedy prose (README rule 3). Only `set_check.extract_regex` is genuinely line-scoped. Each navigator is pinned TWICE because it carries two independent references: the procedural STOP BLOCKED step and the prohibition-list cross-ref; either can be orphaned without the other. The trip-condition pattern (3) is pinned against source prose that is INTENTIONALLY wrapped across five lines in plugin/governance/security-policy.md rather than kept on one line: this is a deliberate standing canary for whitespace-normalized matching (`normalize_ws` in tools/policy_check.sh — see tests/policy/README.md rule 5). If `policy_check.sh` ever regresses from whitespace-normalized matching back to raw substring matching, this pattern stops matching and the fixture fails loudly. DO NOT reflow that sentence onto a single line to tidy it: doing so silently disarms the canary while leaving the fixture green either way, which is worse than deleting the fixture outright.
